identity.title: PaveSplat: Resolution-Robust Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting with Residually Corrected Surface-Aligned Covariances

findings.statement: Feed-forward splats trained at a conventional resolution can expose holes when rerendered at finer sampling rates; surface alignment alone leaves an orientation degree of freedom.
Initialize covariance in a surface-aligned tangent frame, then learn a bounded architectural correction through a residual rotation rather than freely regressing the entire orientation.
Build the frame in camera space from estimated geometry, use it for analytic scales and axes, and predict a residual reorientation on the feed-forward backbone.
Compare native rendering, the High-Resolution Re-Rendering Check on RealEstate10K, and transfer to ScanNet. Train and compare under the common index for the high-resolution condition.

evaluation.gap: Selected experiments transcribed. Other tables and code-level reproduction are outside this record.

findings.statement: Under an identical RealEstate10K recipe, isolate tangent-frame alignment from prediction of the residual orientation; both improve high-resolution PSNR in this ablation.
The residual only adjusts orientation. The design-path ablation covers one backbone and dataset, and unseen-domain transfer remains sensitive to depth quality.
Positions the method between analytic surface alignment and fully learned covariance, using learned residuals to retain geometric structure while adjusting orientation.
Document dataset, common test index, controlled comparisons and statistical conventions.
